summary_en: This study tests hypofractionated radiation therapy combined with a microboost technique in adult men with high-risk, very high-risk, or pelvic lymph node positive prostate cancer. Radiation is given in 25 fractions: the prostate receives 68 Gy, elective lymph nodes receive 45 Gy, and up to three dominant nodules receive a microboost of 70-83 Gy; participation lasts about 6 weeks, with follow-up every three months for two years, then twice yearly for years 3 to 5. The record does not state a primary outcome measure; it is a Phase 2 study that evaluates safety and effectiveness.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la radioterapia hipofraccionada combinada con una técnica de microrrefuerzo (microboost) en hombres adultos con cáncer de próstata de alto riesgo, muy alto riesgo o con ganglios linfáticos pélvicos positivos. La radiación se administra en 25 fracciones: la próstata recibe 68 Gy, los ganglios linfáticos electivos reciben 45 Gy y hasta tres nódulos dominantes reciben un microrrefuerzo de 70-83 Gy; la participación dura aproximadamente 6 semanas, con seguimiento cada tres meses durante dos años y luego dos veces al año en los años 3 a 5. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; es un estudio de fase 2 que evalúa la seguridad y la eficacia.
who_for: Adult men 18 years or older with previously untreated prostate cancer.
High-risk, very high-risk, or pelvic lymph node positive disease without spread outside the pelvic nodes.
Able to have pelvic radiotherapy and prostate or pelvic MRI, with at least one MRI target rated PI-RADS 4 or higher.
Willing and eligible to take long-term androgen deprivation therapy for 12 to 36 months.
not_for: Testosterone supplementation, unless stopped by registration.
Definite evidence of metastatic disease outside the pelvic nodes on conventional imaging.
Prior pelvic radiotherapy, or prior prostate treatment such as total prostatectomy or cryotherapy.
Life expectancy under 5 years or another condition that would preclude curative-intent radiation.
Invasive pelvic or other malignancy within 5 years, unless it is non-melanomatous skin cancer.
